scope: Original server/client error classification and fixed Darwin top-level system aliases only; static review without candidate import, tests, execution or source modification
facts: Remote mapper matches only three exact sanitized code/message pairs generated by original server map_fs_error; both code and message must match. Unknown messages or codes retain original fixed redaction, unsupported and transport paths.

Original INVALID_REQUEST=-32600, INTERNAL=-32603, NOT_FOUND=-32004 match the unchanged server mapping. Oversize remains InvalidData instead of generic Other, and denial remains PermissionDenied instead of generic InvalidInput.

Alias validation requires real root-owned / and /private directories with group/other write bits clear, root-owned actual top-level symlink with exact expected relative or absolute target, and root-owned real target directory. /private/tmp target1777 remains allowed because /private controls its name.

Only /var,/tmp,/etc are transformed into their verified /private counterparts. Policy explicit paths, cwd and supported temporary special paths are folded; mutable descendant symlinks are never resolved to create an allow root.

Original deny matcher is evaluated on kernel path and every inverse verified logical spelling before effective allow check. Invalid globs remain fail-closed, lexical missing denies survive, physical and logical exact/glob/relative deny spellings retain rejection priority. The original deny matcher retains its existing canonical-candidate checks; it is not claimed wholly filesystem-free.

Original stable-handle read, regular-file/nlink checks, expected inode/device, secure O_NOFOLLOW_ANY/O_UNIQUE reopen, F_GETPATH comparison, overflow sentinel, no-prefix bound behavior and entire runtime capability probe are byte-identical. No unsupported capability shortcut or fixture canonicalization was added.
Bazel exec-server uses the existing src/**/*.rs glob through defs.bzl, so the two new src modules fall within the original source set; no build rule change is needed solely to name these modules.
practical_and_security_limits: No Darwin kernel operation or original Mac case was executed by this review. The inferred /var vs/private/var historical runner spelling is still UNKNOWN; a source counterexample is not a historical trace.

UID/mode and symlink checks are not host attestation or a complete Darwin ACL/privilege/mount audit. Admission remains conditional on the original trusted administrator/kernel/system namespace prerequisite; root/admin or an independently compromised namespace is outside this static source claim.
The three new alias tests inject aliases into a private pure helper and do not establish actual filesystem trust checks or native availability. The seven new mapping cases were read but not executed.
All original Windows/security, original Mac integration failures, CI deadlines, cumulative budgets, complete route/model/WAN and merge gates remain unresolved by source-only admission.
